name: get_mcs_ra_mask
prose: Static helper in rtw89 phy.c (lines 53-77) that expands a 16-bit VHT-style MCS map into a 64-bit rate-adaptation mask. It loops over four spatial streams; for stream i it takes the two-bit field (mcs_map >> 2*i) & 3 and ORs into the result, shifted left by 12 * (i + 1), a mask of the low bits 0..highest_mcs when the field is 2, 0..(highest_mcs - gap) when it is 1, and 0..(highest_mcs - 2 * gap) when it is 0 (GENMASK_ULL(n, 0), so n + 1 bits); a field value of 3 contributes nothing. It is pure and has no side effects. highest_mcs - 2 * gap must not be negative for the GENMASK_ULL ranges to be valid.

name: rtw89_phy_ra_sta_update
prose: Builds the rate-adaptation info (rtwsta_link->ra) of a station link for the firmware (rtw89/phy.c:309-486; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It zeroes *ra with memset itself. It collects the capability mask from the station's highest supported PHY (EHT, else HE, else VHT, else HT, each with its own MCS mask, STBC/LDPC flags and, for HE/EHT, GI/LTF handling; csi_mode stays RTW89_RA_RPT_MODE_LEGACY for EHT stations) and adds the legacy rates of the channel band (CCK/OFDM bits for 2.4 GHz, OFDM for 5 and 6 GHz; an unknown band only logs an error and adds nothing). It then trims the mask for the HT-or-higher modes by tx_nss and the sub-OFDM/CCK rates, or for OFDM-only stations, applies the RSSI mask (unless the mode is CCK only), recovers and then ANDs with rtw89_phy_ra_mask_cfg (these steps also run for an unknown band). It sets bw_mode and the SGI flag from the station bandwidth, and dcm_cap from the HE PHY capability. If rtwvif_link->rate_pattern.enable and p2p is false it replaces the mask with the configured mask ANDed with the pattern mask and mode with rate_pattern->ra_mode. It fills ra->bw_cap, er_cap, mode_ctrl, macid, stbc_cap, ldpc_cap, ss_num = min(link_sta->rx_nss, hal.tx_nss) - 1, en_sgi, ra_mask, fix_giltf_en and fix_giltf. If csi is false it returns; otherwise it also sets fixed_csi_rate_en false, ra_csi_rate_en true, cr_tbl_sel false, band_num = phy_idx, csi_bw, csi_gi_ltf, csi_mcs_ss_idx 5 and csi_mode.

name: rtw89_p2p_noa_once_recalc
prose: Recomputes the one-shot P2P notice-of-absence window of a vif link and schedules the set/clear work (real name rtw89_p2p_noa_once_recalc(rtwvif_link), rtw89/ps.c:479-572; returns nothing; the slice shows its second half; the caller holds the wiphy lock, checked with lockdep). It reads the port TSF and returns, after a warning, if that fails. Under rcu_read_lock it dereferences the link's bss_conf and, for each NoA descriptor whose count is neither 0 nor 255 and whose duration is non-zero (and interval non-zero when the count exceeds 1), computes an end time (start + interval * (count - 1) + duration, placed in the current TSF's upper 32 bits) and a start time, skipping descriptors that already ended (end <= tsf), and keeps the earliest begin and the latest end across descriptors. It then leaves the RCU section; if no descriptor was usable (tsf_begin still U64_MAX) it returns without further action. Otherwise it cancels the pending once-work, merges the window with noa_once's stored one if that one has not yet ended, and sets clr_delay_us to the time to the end (capped at UINT_MAX). If tsf_begin <= tsf it marks noa_once->in_duration true and schedules only the clear work; otherwise set_delay_us is the time to the begin, and if it exceeds UINT_MAX it warns, zeroes both delays, sends a beacon-filter config via rtw89_fw_h2c_set_bcn_fltr_cfg(true) and clears in_duration. It queues the set work and the clear work after the respective delays when they are non-zero and stores the window in noa_once->tsf_begin and tsf_end.

name: rtw89_pno_scan_offload
prose: Starts or stops the PNO (scheduled scan) offload of an rtw89 device used for wake-on-WLAN (rtw89/wow.c:1515-1556; static; the slice cut the head). It calls rtw89_mac_scan_offload(rtwdev, &opt, rtwvif_link, true), ignores its return value and returns 0.

name: TRACE_EVENT(queues_stats,
prose: Tracepoint definition for queues_stats(wdev, elected_queue) in the wfx traces.h (line 437); the TRACE_EVENT macro generates the function trace_queues_stats. When the event is recorded, TP_fast_assign initialises all hw, drv and cab counters to -1 and vif_id and queue_id to -1, then iterates over the vifs of wdev and for each of the IEEE80211_NUM_ACS queues stores the pending frame count (queue->pending_frames), the normal queue length and the CAB queue length in the slot vif_id * IEEE80211_NUM_ACS + i (with WARN_ON if the slot is out of range), and records vif_id and queue_id of the queue equal to elected_queue (they stay -1 if elected_queue is NULL or matches none). The text format prints 'got skb from vif/queue' and the three counters for the eight slots. It does not modify wdev or the queues.

name: cw1200_wow_suspend
prose: Prepares a cw1200 device for WoWLAN suspend (cw1200/pm.c:157-302; the slice cut the head). It returns -EAGAIN if the stay-awake timer is pending, -EBUSY if the TX queue has queued frames, and -EBUSY if conf_mutex cannot be taken with mutex_trylock. With the mutex held it goes to revert1 (unlock and return -EBUSY) if a channel switch or join is in progress or scan.lock cannot be taken with down_trylock. It locks TX asynchronously and waits up to HZ/10 for the hardware buffers to drain (otherwise revert2). It sets the UDP-port and ether-type filters, allocates the suspend state (failure: revert3), and, for a non-P2P STA in a mode other than legacy PS, switches to legacy PS and waits up to 1 s for the switch (timeout: revert4). It stores and suspends four delayed works, cancels clear_recent_scan_work, may enable beacon skipping, suspends the bh thread (failure: revert5) and fails to revert6 if the mcast timeout is pending. It stores the state in pm_state->suspend_state and calls hwbus_ops->power_mgmt(true); if that fails it logs, calls cw1200_wow_resume, unlocks conf_mutex and returns -EBUSY; if atomic bh_rx shows a pending RX event it calls cw1200_wow_resume, unlocks conf_mutex and returns -EAGAIN. Otherwise it returns 0 with conf_mutex still held (released by the resume path). The revert labels fall through: revert6 resumes the bh thread, revert5 resumes the four delayed works, revert4 frees the state, revert3 restores the UDP and ether-type filters, revert2 unlocks TX and releases scan.lock, revert1 unlocks conf_mutex; each returns -EBUSY.

name: cw1200_rx_cb
prose: RX handler of the cw1200 driver (real name cw1200_rx_cb(priv, arg, link_id, skb_p), cw1200/txrx.c:1014-1234; returns nothing; the slice shows only its body). It works on the skb at *skb_p and takes ownership only when it passes the frame to mac80211 (it then sets *skb_p = NULL); on every drop path it returns leaving *skb_p set, so the caller still owns and frees the skb. It drops the frame if the interface mode is unspecified, if arg->status is WSM_STATUS_NO_KEY_FOUND or any failure other than a MIC failure (a MIC failure only sets RX_FLAG_MMIC_ERROR), if the frame is shorter than a PS-Poll, if cw1200_handle_pspoll handles a PS-Poll, or if the encryption type is unknown or the frame is shorter than the header plus IV and ICV. In AP mode it marks soft-state link entries to buffer early data and updates the link timestamp; for P2P public action frames it records the source address and schedules linkid_reset_work (with a WARN_ON if it is already pending). It fills band, frequency, rate index, signal and antenna in the rx status, removes IV, ICV/MIC and, if included, the trailing 8-byte TSF (stored in mactime), handles action frames (cw1200_handle_action_rx; if it returns non-zero the function returns with the skb left owned by the caller... as written, returning without clearing *skb_p) and, for beacons from the joined BSS with status 0, updates the DTIM period (queuing set_beacon_wakeup_period_work) and may disable the beacon filter. It calls cw1200_pm_stay_awake with 5 s for auth/deauth frames and 1 s otherwise, and delivers the skb with ieee80211_rx_irqsafe, or queues it on the link's rx_queue under ps_state_lock if it is early data for a still-soft link.

name: wl1251_op_configure_filter
prose: mac80211 configure_filter callback of wl1251 (ti/wl1251/main.c:757-824; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). multicast is a pointer to a wl1251_filter_params (or 0) which the function frees with kfree on every path. It masks *total and changed with WL1251_SUPPORTED_FILTERS; if no supported filter bit changed it frees fp and returns without touching the device. Otherwise it takes wl->mutex, resets wl->rx_config and wl->rx_filter to their defaults and applies FIF_ALLMULTI, FCSFAIL, BCN_PRBRESP_PROMISC, CONTROL, OTHER_BSS (or an all-zero bssid) and PROBE_REQ to them. If the device is off it goes to the exit. Otherwise it wakes the chip from ELP (a negative result goes to the exit), sends the group address table (empty with FIF_ALLMULTI, or from fp if fp is non-NULL; a negative result goes to the exit without putting the chip back to sleep), sends the RX config with wl1251_acx_rx_config (its return value is ignored) and then calls wl1251_ps_elp_sleep. At the exit it unlocks wl->mutex and frees fp.

name: mac80211_hwsim_tx_frame_nl
prose: Forwards a TX frame of a mac80211_hwsim radio to user space (wmediumd) as a netlink message (mac80211_hwsim.c:1525-1635; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). If data->ps is not PS_DISABLED it sets the PM bit in the frame's frame_control. If the pending queue holds MAX_QUEUE or more skbs it dequeues and frees skbs with ieee80211_free_txskb (counting data->tx_dropped) until fewer than WARN_QUEUE remain. It then allocates a generic netlink message and puts the transmitter address, the frame, the translated TX flags, the channel frequency, the TX rate and rate-flag arrays and, last, a cookie: the cookie is obtained from atomic_inc_return(&data->pending_cookie) and stored in info->rate_driver_data[0] before the cookie attribute is put. Any allocation or nla_put failure frees the message and goes to the error exit. On success it sends the message with hwsim_tx_virtio (if hwsim_virtio_enabled) or hwsim_unicast_netgroup to dst_portid; if that fails it goes to the error exit. Success queues my_skb on data->pending and updates tx_pkts and tx_bytes; the error exit frees my_skb with ieee80211_free_txskb and increments data->tx_failed. my_skb is thus either queued or freed, exactly once, in every case.

name: __t7xx_pci_pm_resume
prose: Resume handler of the t7xx PCIe modem driver (t7xx_pci.c:572-676; static; the slice cut the head). If md_pm_state is at most MTK_PM_INIT it enables ASPM L1 low-power and returns 0 without changing md_pm_state. Otherwise it enables the PCIe MAC interrupts and reads the previous PM state register. If state_check is true: a previous state of L3, or INIT with an invalid ATR source address, calls t7xx_pci_reprobe_early (a non-zero result is returned) and returns t7xx_pci_reprobe(t7xx_dev, true), without setting md_pm_state to MTK_PM_RESUMED; EXP or L2_EXP (after a t7xx_pcie_reinit that, for L2_EXP, returns its error on failure) set md_pm_state to MTK_PM_SUSPENDED, enable the SAP RGU interrupt, unmask the exception and port-enum MHCCIF interrupts and return ret (0 unless the reinit failed); L2 calls t7xx_pcie_reinit (error returned) and then continues with the normal resume; any other state except L1 and INIT sends FSM_CMD_STOP (error returned), clears the RGU IRQ, sets md_pm_state to MTK_PM_SUSPENDED and returns 0. The normal path disables ASPM low-power, waits for the PM config, runs each entity's resume_early, sends the H2D_CH_RESUME_REQ and H2D_CH_RESUME_REQ_AP PM requests (errors only logged), runs each entity's resume callback, logging errors, so that ret ends up as the status of the last resume callback run (or of the last PM request if no entity has a resume callback), enables the SAP RGU interrupt, re-enables ASPM low-power, marks runtime-PM busy, sets md_pm_state to MTK_PM_RESUMED and returns ret.

name: apple_nvme_reset_work
prose: Reset work of the Apple NVMe (ANS) controller (apple.c:1038-1234; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It requires the controller state to be NVME_CTRL_RESETTING (else it records -ENODEV and takes the failure exit) and fails with -EIO if RTKit has crashed. If RTKit is running it disables the controller if enabled, shuts RTKit down (an error goes to the failure exit) and clears the coprocessor CPU control register; if the coprocessor CPU is then not running it asserts the reset line, reinitialises RTKit, deasserts the reset, starts the CPU and boots RTKit, otherwise it wakes RTKit (a non-zero result is an error). It polls the boot-status register for APPLE_ANS_BOOT_STATUS_OK. It then sets the transfer limits, programs the linear queue/NVMMU registers if the hardware has them, the admin queue registers, enables the controller (nvme_enable_ctrl), starts the admin queue, moves the controller to CONNECTING (-ENODEV on failure), and runs nvme_init_ctrl_finish, apple_nvme_create_cq and apple_nvme_create_sq. It then requests one I/O queue with nvme_set_queue_count (a failure, or a count other than 1 giving -ENXIO, removes the queues created so far), updates the tag set to one hardware queue, moves the controller to LIVE (-ENODEV on failure) and starts it. The status code ret is only used for a log message 'Reset failure status'. On any failure it removes the SQ and CQ if they were created, moves the controller to NVME_CTRL_DELETING, takes a controller reference, disables the controller, marks the namespaces dead and queues remove_work on nvme_wq, dropping the extra reference if the work was already queued.

name: nvmf_parse_options
prose: Parses the comma/newline separated 'key=value' option string for an NVMe-oF controller into *opts (nvme/host/fabrics.c:715-1123; static; the slice cut the head). It sets defaults (queue size, I/O queue count = online CPUs, reconnect delay, kato 0, tos -1, no digests, no TLS) and duplicates buf (-ENOMEM on failure; the copy is freed on every path). The default host id and NQN are used unless overridden. Each recognised option updates opts (and opts->mask): string options replace the stored string (-ENOMEM on allocation failure); the subsystem NQN must be shorter than NVMF_NQN_SIZE and sets discovery_nqn when it equals the discovery name; queue_size must be within the min/max, nr_io_queues, reconnect_delay, nr_write_queues and nr_poll_queues must be positive; kato must be non-negative (0 is allowed with a warning); ctrl_loss_tmo may be negative (meaning reconnect forever, with a warning); fail_fast_tmo values below 0 become -1; tos must be non-negative and values above 255 are clamped to 255 with a warning; hostnqn after a user-assigned host returns -EADDRINUSE and one that is too long -EINVAL; hostid must parse as a UUID; keyring and tls_key take a key id (-EINVAL if not positive, or the error from nvmf_parse_key); DH-CHAP secrets must be at least 11 characters starting with 'DHHC-1:' (-EINVAL); tls and concat require CONFIG_NVME_TCP_TLS (-EINVAL otherwise); a failed numeric parse or unknown option gives -EINVAL. After the loop, discovery controllers get zero I/O queues and duplicate_connect true, others default kato to NVME_DEFAULT_KATO; max_reconnects is -1 for a negative ctrl_loss_tmo else ctrl_loss_tmo divided by reconnect_delay rounded up; secure concatenation with TLS or a TLS key, or without a DH-CHAP secret, returns -EINVAL. Finally it calls nvmf_host_add(hostnqn, &hostid) and stores the result in opts->host (its error is returned, with opts->host reset to NULL). On error returns opts may be partly updated and what it already stored stays owned by opts.

name: nvmet_execute_auth_send
prose: Handles an NVMe-oF AUTH_SEND command on the target side (real name nvmet_execute_auth_send(req), nvme/target/fabrics-cmd-auth.c:251-423; returns nothing). It rejects with NVME_SC_INVALID_FIELD | NVME_STATUS_DNR (and sets req->error_loc to the offending field) when secp is not the DH-CHAP protocol id, spsp0 or spsp1 is not 0x01, or the transfer length tl is 0, and goes to the common completion. If nvmet_check_transfer_len(req, tl) rejects the length it returns at once without completing the request here (that helper completes it). It allocates tl bytes (NVME_SC_INTERNAL on failure) and copies the payload from the SGL (a non-zero status from nvmet_copy_from_sgl goes to completion with that status). It then dispatches on the message type and the current sq->dhchap_step: a type that is neither common nor DH-CHAP messages, or an id not matching the expected step, sets dhchap_status INCORRECT_MESSAGE and step FAILURE2; a NEGOTIATE common message (restarting authentication, on queue 0 re-running nvmet_setup_auth) validates the negotiation and moves the step to CHALLENGE or FAILURE1 with the status; a DH-CHAP message with a wrong transaction id sets FAILURE1 with INCORRECT_PAYLOAD; REPLY runs nvmet_auth_reply (step SUCCESS1 or FAILURE1); SUCCESS2 marks the sq authenticated (inserting the PSK for concatenation); FAILURE2 runs nvmet_auth_failure2 and records the failure and clears authenticated; any other id sets INCORRECT_MESSAGE, step FAILURE2 and clears authenticated. It frees the payload, then, if the step is neither SUCCESS2 nor FAILURE2, re-arms the auth expiry delayed work (kato or 120 s); otherwise it frees the sq auth state and, for FAILURE2, calls nvmet_ctrl_fatal_error. It completes the request with nvmet_req_complete(req, status), where status is 0 unless one of the NVMe errors above applied (DH-CHAP failures are carried in the sq state, not in status).

name: nvmet_install_queue
prose: Attaches the SQ/CQ of an NVMe-oF connect command to a controller (nvme/target/fabrics-cmd.c:172-243; static, returns a u16 NVMe status; the slice cut the head). It takes qid and sqsize from the connect command and checks them in this order, returning an error status for each: sqsize == 0 returns NVME_SC_CONNECT_INVALID_PARAM | NVME_STATUS_DNR with req->error_loc at sqsize and the result field set (and sets req->sq->ctrl = NULL through the err label); ctrl->sqs[qid] already set returns NVME_SC_CMD_SEQ_ERROR | DNR with error_loc at qid; for qid != 0, sqsize larger than the controller's MQES returns CONNECT_INVALID_PARAM | DNR with error_loc at sqsize. name: shpc_init
prose: Initialises a PCI standard hot-plug controller (SHPC) (shpchp_hpc.c:873-1048; the slice cut the head). It sets ctrl->pci_dev and determines the register window: for the AMD GOLAM 7450 it assumes base offset 0 and uses BAR 0; otherwise it requires the SHPC capability (failing with rc -1 if absent), reads the base offset, slot count and creg registers through shpc_indirect_read (their error returned) and sets mmio_base/mmio_size from the base offset and slot count. It enables the device (error returned), reserves the MMIO region and ioremaps it (failure of either returns -1; after a failed ioremap the region is released), and initialises crit_sect, cmd_lock and the wait queue. It reads the slot configuration into the controller (first device offset, slot count, first slot number, numbering direction), masks the global, command-complete and arbiter SERR interrupts and, for each slot, the event and SERR masks. In poll mode (shpchp_poll_mode) it sets up the polling timer with a 10 s first delay; otherwise it tries pci_enable_msi (falling back to INTx with a message), sets bus mastering if MSI was enabled and requests the shared IRQ shpc_isr (on failure it iounmaps creg and returns that error without releasing the memory region or disabling the device). It reads the maximum and current bus speed, unmasks the slot event interrupts for all slots and, when not polling, the global and command interrupts, and returns 0. All the other failure paths return the error without undoing the pci_enable_device or the reserved memory region (except the ioremap case).

name: pci_pm_suspend_noirq
prose: noirq suspend handler of the PCI core (pci-driver.c:877-971; static; the slice cut the head). It returns 0 at once if dev_pm_skip_suspend(dev), and returns pci_legacy_suspend_late(dev) for a device with legacy PM support. If the driver has no pm ops it saves the PCI state and goes to the set_unknown step. If the driver has a suspend_noirq callback it calls it; a non-zero result is returned immediately (no fixup, may_skip_resume unchanged). If after a successful callback the state was not saved and the device is neither in D0 nor PCI_UNKNOWN, it goes straight to the Fixup step (skipping the save and set_unknown steps), issuing a one-time warning only if current_state differs from its value before the callback. Otherwise, if the state is not yet saved, it saves it and, if skip_bus_pm is false and the device is power manageable, calls pci_prepare_to_sleep. If current_state is then D0 it sets skip_bus_pm on the device and on its parent bridge (if any). If skip_bus_pm is set and the platform is not involved in suspend it goes to Fixup. Otherwise (set_unknown) it marks the power state unknown and, for a USB EHCI class device, writes 0 to PCI_COMMAND. Fixup runs pci_fixup_device(pci_fixup_suspend_late) and clears dev->power.may_skip_resume when the device can wake the system but wakeup is not enabled. It returns 0 on those paths.

name: pci_request_region
prose: Exported wrapper (pci.c:3869-3872) that reserves one BAR of a PCI device by calling the static helper __pci_request_region(pdev, bar, name, 0) and returning its result. The helper returns -EINVAL if bar is not a valid BAR index, returns 0 without reserving anything if the BAR's length is 0 (or if the BAR's flags are neither I/O nor memory), reserves an I/O BAR with request_region and a memory BAR with __request_mem_region (non-exclusive), and returns -EBUSY after a warning if that reservation fails; otherwise 0.
note: [rev:right] r1 (returns 0 without reserving a zero-length or unflagged BAR) right: pci.c:3832-3833, 3835-3846

name: pci_release_selected_regions
prose: Exported function (pci.c:3883-3890) that releases the BARs selected by the bitmask bars: for each bit i set in bars with i below PCI_STD_NUM_BARS it calls pci_release_region(pdev, i). Bits at or above PCI_STD_NUM_BARS are ignored. It returns nothing.
note: [rev:right] r1 (ignores bits >= PCI_STD_NUM_BARS) right: pci.c:3887-3889

name: __pci_request_selected_regions
prose: Static helper (pci.c:3893-3910) that reserves the BARs selected by the bitmask bars. For each bit i set (below PCI_STD_NUM_BARS) it calls __pci_request_region(pdev, i, name, excl); a BAR with zero length counts as success without reserving anything. If any call fails it releases, with pci_release_region, the selected BARs below the failing index (including any whose request was a no-op for zero length) and returns -EBUSY (whatever the helper's error was); otherwise it returns 0.
note: [rev:right] r1 (zero-length BARs can return success without reservation) right: pci.c:3832-3833 via 3900; the failure return is always -EBUSY: 3909

name: pci_request_selected_regions
prose: Exported wrapper (pci.c:3921-3925) returning __pci_request_selected_regions(pdev, bars, name, 0): it reserves the selected BARs non-exclusively; it returns 0 on success (zero-length BARs are skipped without a reservation) and -EBUSY, after releasing those it had reserved, if any request fails.
note: [rev:right] r1 (zero-length BARs can return success without reservation) right: pci.c:3832-3833

name: pci_request_selected_regions_exclusive
prose: Exported wrapper (pci.c:3936-3941) returning __pci_request_selected_regions(pdev, bars, name, IORESOURCE_EXCLUSIVE). The exclusive flag is only passed on for memory BARs (via __request_mem_region); I/O BARs are still reserved with the plain request_region and so are not exclusive. It returns 0 on success (zero-length BARs are skipped) and -EBUSY, after releasing the BARs reserved so far, if any request fails.
note: [rev:right] r1 (I/O BARs are not requested exclusively) right: pci.c:3835-3843

name: pci_request_regions
prose: Exported wrapper (pci.c:3971-3975) that reserves all standard BARs of a PCI device by calling pci_request_selected_regions(pdev, (1 << PCI_STD_NUM_BARS) - 1, name): it returns 0 on success (zero-length BARs are skipped without a reservation) and -EBUSY if a BAR cannot be reserved, after releasing the ones already reserved.
note: [rev:right] r1 (zero-length BARs can return success without reservation) right: pci.c:3832-3833

name: pci_request_regions_exclusive
prose: Exported wrapper (pci.c:3995-3999) that reserves all standard BARs by calling pci_request_selected_regions_exclusive(pdev, (1 << PCI_STD_NUM_BARS) - 1, name): memory BARs are reserved exclusively but I/O BARs are not (they use the plain request_region); zero-length BARs are skipped; it returns 0 on success and -EBUSY, after releasing what it had reserved, otherwise.
note: [rev:right] r1 (I/O BARs are not requested exclusively) right: pci.c:3835-3843

name: pci_register_io_range
prose: Registers a CPU MMIO window as a logical PIO range (pci.c:4006-4035). Without PCI_IOBASE it does nothing and returns 0. With PCI_IOBASE it returns -EINVAL if size is 0 or addr + size wraps, allocates a logic_pio_hwaddr with GFP_ATOMIC (-ENOMEM on failure), fills fwnode, size, hw_start and flags LOGIC_PIO_CPU_MMIO and calls logic_pio_register_range; if that fails it frees the node and returns its error, except that -EEXIST is turned into 0.
note: [rev:right] r1 (without PCI_IOBASE it returns 0 without registering) right: pci.c:4009-4010, 4032-4034

name: pci_pio_to_address
prose: Converts a logical I/O port number to a CPU physical address (pci.c:4037-4045; exported GPL). With PCI_IOBASE and pio below MMIO_UPPER_LIMIT it returns logic_pio_to_hwaddr(pio); in all other cases (no PCI_IOBASE, or pio not below the limit) it returns OF_BAD_ADDR cast to phys_addr_t. It has no side effects.
note: [rev:right] r1 (the formal contract omitted the pio >= MMIO_UPPER_LIMIT path) right; contract left empty: pci.c:4040-4044

name: pci_remap_iospace
prose: Maps a PCI I/O port resource into the kernel virtual address space (pci.c:4071-4092). With PCI_IOBASE it returns -EINVAL if res is not an IORESOURCE_IO resource or res->end exceeds IO_SPACE_LIMIT; otherwise it returns the result of vmap_page_range(PCI_IOBASE + res->start, ... + resource_size(res), phys_addr, pgprot_device(PAGE_KERNEL)), which is 0 on success or a negative errno (for example -ENOMEM) on failure. Without PCI_IOBASE it warns once and returns -ENODEV.
